chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from one whom he mentioned, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The blood-money of the fetus is five portions: one-fifth for the drop of fluid, twenty dīnārs; for the clot, two-fifths, forty dīnārs; for the lump of flesh, three-fifths, sixty dīnārs; for the bone, four-fifths, eighty dīnārs. When the fetus is complete, it is one hundred dīnārs. When the spirit is produced in it, then its blood-money is one thousand dīnārs, or ten thousand dirhams, if it is male; and if it is female, then five hundred dīnārs. If a woman is killed while she is pregnant, and it is not known whether her child was male or female, then its blood-money for the child is in two halves: half of the blood-money of a male and half of the blood-money of a female; and her blood-money is complete.

key_terms.الرُّوحُ: the spirit, whose emergence marks a higher legal valuation
key_terms.النُّطْفَةِ: the seminal drop or earliest embryonic stage
key_terms.الْعَلَقَةِ: the clinging clot stage of embryonic development
key_terms.الْمُضْغَةِ: the chewed-like lump stage of embryonic development
key_terms.دِينَاراً: a dinar, the unit used here for legal compensation
key_terms.دِيَةُ: financial compensation due for wrongful killing or injury

ai.seo_question: What is the dīyah for a fetus at different stages of development in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out detailed legal rulings for the dīyah of a fetus at different stages of development, assigning specific amounts according to its formation. It also gives the ruling for a pregnant woman who is killed, including how the unborn child's compensation is calculated when the sex is unknown.
